cat <<'EOF' | tee .program/audits/ROOT.1.1.3-adversarial-review.md
# Adversarial Review: ROOT.1.1.3 (REQ-CP-05 revisions module)

Artifact: src/lib/revisions.ts, tests/revisions.test.ts, content/migrations/README.md, content/migrations/example-migration.json
Spec basis: .program/spec/content-pipeline.md REQ-CP-05
Reviewer: dream-reviewer-adversarial (dry-run generation, real review)
Date: 2026-07-27

Baseline: npx vitest run tests/revisions.test.ts passed 21/21 before probing.

## Findings

### F1 (BLOCKING) Canonicalization silently collapses distinct contents, breaking "content change flips hash"

Spec passage violated (REQ-CP-05 scenario 1): "Given an item whose content changes in any way, when the bundle rebuilds, then its itemRevision hash changes while its item ID does not."
Contract clause violated: "canonical-JSON sorted-keys SHA-256" -- the serializer does not produce canonical JSON for non-plain values and never rejects them.

Empirical results (node --experimental-strip-types probe, importing computeItemRevision):

- NaN===null? true; Infinity===null? true; NaN===Infinity? true
  JSON.stringify(NaN) and JSON.stringify(Infinity) both yield the string null, so a content edit changing a numeric field from NaN or Infinity to literal null (or between NaN and Infinity) does NOT change the hash. Distinct contents, identical revision. Direct scenario-1 violation.
- Date===emptyObj? true; Map===emptyObj? true; Set===emptyObj? true
  Dates, Maps and Sets have no own enumerable keys, so canonicalStringify (revisions.ts lines 131-143) serializes all of them as an empty object. Any change to a Date value or Map/Set contents leaves the hash unchanged. The compiled-content path today feeds JSON-parsed data, but the signature is content: unknown and the beat compiler builds objects in JS where a Date can appear unnoticed.
- toJSON is ignored: an object with a toJSON method hashes by its raw own keys, diverging from JSON.stringify semantics that the doc comment (line 116) claims to match.
- Function-valued keys are NOT omitted: canonicalStringify hits the line-146 fallback, JSON.stringify(fn) returns the value undefined, and the canonical string contains the literal token undefined -- not valid JSON, contradicting both the doc comment ("matching JSON.stringify semantics"; JSON.stringify omits function-valued keys) and the canonical-JSON contract. Probed: objWithFn===objWithout? false.
- Top-level function input crashes with a misleading crypto error ("data argument must be of type string... Received undefined"); BigInt crashes with a serializer error; circular references crash with a bare RangeError (stack overflow), not a diagnosable message.
- Top-level undefined hashes the 9-char string undefined (again not JSON).

Why two prior reviews would miss it: every test in tests/revisions.test.ts feeds plain JSON-safe literals; the module reads fluently and the doc comments assert the exact properties the code lacks.

Fix direction: either validate input is JSON-representable (throw with a clear message on NaN/Infinity/BigInt/function/Date/Map/Set/circular) or canonicalize them explicitly. Silence is the bug; either explicit behavior satisfies scenario 1.

### F2 (should-fix) Migration entry validation accepts entries that cannot "link old revision to new"

Spec passage (REQ-CP-05 scenario 2): "a migration map entry exists linking old revision to new."
README contract (content/migrations/README.md): fromRevision/toRevision are "the 16-character hex hash".

Empirical results (fixture probes under .program/audits/ROOT.1.1.3-verification/fx1..fx7):

- empty-string itemId/fromRevision/toRevision/note: PASSES validation.
- non-hex, wrong-length revisions (not-a-hash!!, ZZZ): PASSES validation.
- fromRevision identical to toRevision (no-op entry): PASSES.
- two entries with the same {itemId, fromRevision} pointing at DIFFERENT toRevisions (fx4, across two files): PASSES, both returned. A downstream consumer resolving an attempt recorded against the old revision now has an ambiguous, unresolvable mapping -- the map no longer links old to new, it forks.

The zod schema (revisions.ts lines 12-17) is four bare z.string() fields. Minimum hardening: nonempty, 16-char lowercase-hex regex for the two revision fields, reject fromRevision === toRevision, and reject duplicate {itemId, fromRevision} pairs across the whole load. The README documents the hex format; the code does not enforce its own README.

### F3 (should-fix) buildRevisionsMap silently loses an item whose id is __proto__

Contract clause: buildRevisionsMap(items) returns Record with one entry per unique id, throwing only on duplicates.
Empirical result: buildRevisionsMap([{id:'__proto__',...},{id:'constructor',...}]) returned a map whose only own key is constructor; the __proto__ entry vanished (assignment at line 54 hits the prototype accessor, not an own property). No throw, no pollution (probed: Object polluted? false), just silent data loss -- an item id that never appears in the revisions map, so its content changes are invisible downstream. Fix: use a null-prototype object or a Map internally.

### F4 (should-fix) loadMigrationMaps output order is platform-dependent and ENOENT is silent on caller-supplied dirs

readdirSync order is filesystem-dependent, so the returned MigrationEntry[] ordering is not deterministic across platforms -- relevant if CP-04 hashes or snapshots the migration set into the immutable bundle. Also, a typo in a caller-supplied dir returns [] silently (line 74-77); the ENOENT-tolerant default is reasonable for the default path only. Distinguish: default dir missing may return [], explicit dir missing should throw.

### F5 (note) Tests assert weaker properties than the requirement

- The batch-load test (tests/revisions.test.ts lines 193-221) uses toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2) and .some(...) -- it cannot fail if the loader duplicates entries or leaks entries from other files.
- Determinism tests only recompute in the same process; nothing falsifies cross-process/cross-platform stability (held in practice -- see below -- but the test name overclaims).
- The undefined-omission test (lines 92-101) pins implementation behavior, not a spec scenario; fine, but it is the only canonicalization edge probed at all.

### F6 (note) 16-hex truncation fitness for CP-04 -- examined and HELD

64 bits of SHA-256. Birthday collision probability at 100,000 items is about 2.7e-10 (computed in probe). A collision would silently mark changed content unchanged, but at content-bank scale this is acceptable; no finding. Worth one code comment stating the accepted bound.

## Searched and held

1. Structure-injection via crafted strings (keys or values containing quote/comma/brace sequences): held -- strings pass through JSON.stringify so delimiters cannot be forged; probed injection distinct? true.
2. Unicode NFC vs NFD forms of the same glyph hash differently (probed: NFC===NFD? false is expected canonical-JSON behavior since RFC 8785 does not normalize; both forms are distinct code points): treated as correct, not a finding.
3. itemRevision leaking onto the compiled Beat shape (sidecar rule): held -- src/lib/beats.ts documents no itemRevision field and grep shows only beats.ts/revisions.ts mention it.
4. Prototype pollution via migration JSON files containing __proto__ keys: held -- zod safeParse output and JSON.parse do not pollute; probed Object polluted? false.

- node --experimental-strip-types --input-type=module probes (canonicalization edge cases; output above)
- fixture-based loadMigrationMaps probes against .program/audits/ROOT.1.1.3-verification/fx1..fx7

### NEW-1 (major) - Sparse-array holes bypass the domain check and silently collapse

elements are not object values).

  acceptance criteria and both scoping calls; results quoted per criterion below.

## Per-criterion findings

AC1 â€” non-plain arrays rejected. PASS. isPlainArray requires getPrototypeOf identically
the Array prototype, and it is applied BEFORE any iteration, so no partial
canonicalization occurs. Probe: an Array subclass instance throws TypeError naming
"(root)" and the class name; an array whose prototype was reassigned to null throws
naming the null-prototype reassignment case. Both messages carry a JSON path.

AC2 â€” own symbol keys and non-index enumerable own properties rejected. PASS. Probe: a
symbol-keyed array throws with path "(root)[Symbol(s)]" and the text "symbol-keyed
property on an array"; an enumerable expando holding a Date throws naming the key and
"non-index enumerable own property". The symbol check is textually the array-arm mirror of
the object arm's existing symbol check, satisfying the "matching the object arm" clause.
The canonical-index predicate is correctly strict â€” it rejects "01", "1.0", "-0", "+1",
"1e0" and a leading-space key, none of which are element slots â€” and the tests cover the
two genuinely tricky JS cases (a numeric key inside index range extends length and
therefore surfaces as the more specific HOLE diagnosis; a key past 2^32-1 does not extend
length and is caught as non-index). That is documented-by-test rather than assumed.

AC3 â€” all ten pins unchanged, by value and by text. PASS, see independent re-derivation
above. The fix is rejection-only by construction: both new gates return through
rejectOutOfDomain before any part string is produced, so they cannot alter the canonical
string of any admitted input. Probe confirms plain literals, Array-from output, spread
output, JSON-parsed arrays, frozen arrays and sealed arrays all still hash to the pinned
pair value.

AC4 â€” rejection tests with paths for both defects. PASS. GEN2-1 block: 7 tests (re-pinned
collision partners; subclass at root; subclass at a nested path; two distinct subclasses
throwing rather than colliding with each other; null-prototype reassignment; positive
admission set; object-arm symmetry). GEN2-2 block: 11 tests (symbol key; Date expando;
function expando; self-reference expando â€” the undetected cycle; in-domain-valued expando
proving the rule is structural not a value check; nested path; index-looking keys; the
length-extension hole case; the beyond-index-range case; the deliberate non-enumerable
tolerance; holes still reported as holes). 18 new tests total, matching the stated count.
Every rejection assertion checks TypeError, not-RangeError, path containment AND a
descriptor regex, so a throw for the wrong reason fails the test.

AC5 â€” PASS (npm test exit 0, tsc exit 0; lint unaffected).

HARD INVARIANT, exported signatures. PASS. Three exports remain, all typeof function,
all arity 1, all with constructor name "Function" (not AsyncFunction) â€” still synchronous.
The migration-entry type export is unchanged. tsc exit 0 with the unmodified consumer test
file is corroborating evidence.

HARD INVARIANT, object arm and hole/depth/cycle logic untouched. PASS on the evidence
available to me (I do not run git). The hole check is still an explicit index-based "in"
test, never hole-skipping iteration (A1-1 normative implementation constraint honoured);
the depth guard is still an explicit counter firing at depth greater than 64; cycle
detection is still the ancestors set with a finally-scoped delete, so sibling-shared
references stay legal. Probe: depth 64 hashes, depth 65 throws with a path and the
"MAX_HASH_DEPTH 64" text and is not a RangeError; a one-slot sparse array throws naming
index 0. All 96 pre-existing tests pass unchanged, which is the strongest available
behavioral proof that no pre-existing branch shifted.

One ordering point I checked because it could have been a silent regression: the non-index
check runs BEFORE the density loop, so a sparse array could in principle have been
re-diagnosed as "non-index property" instead of "array hole". It is not, because a hole
means FEWER own index keys than length rather than an extra key, so the enumerable-key
scan finds nothing to complain about and the hole loop still produces the more specific
message. Verified by probe and by two dedicated tests.

## Scoping call (a) â€” narrow GEN2-2: non-ENUMERABLE own properties on arrays tolerated

RULING: consistent-with-spec, with a MINOR residual noted below.

Reading adopted: A1-3's closed world is a rule about the VALUE BEING HASHED, and
ADR-0017 fixes that value as "the JSON data model". Non-enumerable own properties are
invisible to that model â€” and, decisively for symmetry, the object arm ratified in the
closed predecessor item already tolerates them. My probe confirms the object arm's
leniency independently: a plain object carrying a non-enumerable Date hashes, and so does
one carrying a non-enumerable self-reference. The narrow form therefore makes the two arms
EXACTLY symmetric, which is the property the disposition's reading-1 argument rested on
(same condition, same value class, same outcome). The strict form would have created a
fresh opposite-direction asymmetry, which the disposition itself flagged and explicitly
delegated as "a scoping call for the fix item, not a spec question". The implementation
also states the choice and its reason in-comment and pins it with a test rather than
leaving it as an accident of the predicate. That is the right disposition of a delegated
call.

MINOR (not blocking, not a regression, and NOT this item's to fix): the scenario-3
OUTCOME prohibition is still reachable through a non-enumerable own property in BOTH
arms â€” probe shows a Date and a self-reference both hashing silently that way. This is a
pre-existing property of the object arm, symmetric after this fix rather than widened by
it, and closing it would change nothing about the pins. Recommend the Phase 0 gate carry
it as a separate one-line observation on the object arm, not against this item.

words. ADR-0017's reject list reads "class instances (non-plain prototypes incl.

admission is scoped to the Object-create-with-null idiom; a null-prototype ARRAY can only
arise from setPrototypeOf on an existing array, which is precisely the "accident beyond"
that the same clause rejects. There is no null-prototype-array idiom and JSON parsing
never produces one, so nothing in the real hash-input domain is lost. The module states
this reasoning at the predicate, and a test pins it. Both arms are also verified reachable
in the right order: the isArray branch precedes the plain-object branch, so a
null-prototype array cannot slip into the lenient object arm.

# ROOT.7.3.7 fix-verify -- ADR-0025 (REQ-EX-01 s3 no-driver-branching)

Reviewer: dream-reviewer-primary, FRESH instance, blind. Lens: spec conformance.
Date: 2026-07-27. Tooling: ripgrep 14.1.1 (+pcre2).
VERDICT: request_changes, confidence high.

Scope read: the shard REQ-EX-01 s3 (line 21), the artifact ADR-0025, the gen0 review,
and the verification evidence dir. Item file NOT read. git NOT run (reviewer constraint).

## Finding 1 -- EXECUTABLE PROCEDURE: DISCHARGED

Ran all 11 command lines from the ADR body character-for-character against src.
Every one exits 1 with zero hits. The bad rg file-type argument is gone (no occurrence
of that token anywhere in the ADR). Recorded transcript at ADR lines 116-126 matches
reproducible reality exactly.

## Finding 2 -- PATTERN COMPLETENESS: NOT DISCHARGED

Two independent defects.

### 2a. Cited evidence contradicts the ADR body, and the reusable runner is broken

ADR line 140 claims CHECK 8 caught 1 hit at line 71. The evidence file it cites,
the negative-control run log, records at its line 46:

    === CHECK 8: switch on driver.name ===
    Exit: 1

i.e. NO hit. Root cause: the runner script line 57 uses a narrower CHECK 8 regex than
the ADR body line 73. Reproduced against the negative control:

    runner regex   -> exit 1 (misses)
    ADR body regex -> exit 0, hits lines 69 and 71

The runner's driver-substring clause cannot match the switch on activeDriver.name
because rg is case-sensitive and the receiver has a capital D. So: the ADR body's own
command is sound, but (i) the pasted per-check evidence is not supported by the saved
artifact it points at, and (ii) the runner script -- the very script ROOT.4.5 and the
ROOT.4.9 gate row are bound to re-run -- silently under-detects mechanism 8. Same class
as gen0 finding 1: recorded procedure diverges from reality.

Evidence to satisfy: runner CHECK 8 aligned to the ADR body command, script re-run, the
negative-control run log regenerated showing CHECK 8 exit 0, and the ADR body per-check
hit list reconciled line-for-line against the regenerated log.

### 2b. All 10 gen0 mechanisms ARE caught -- but 8 NEW mechanisms escape

Ran the ADR's 11 commands over the negative control myself: all exit 0. Every one of the
10 gen0-identified mechanisms is now detected. That half of finding 2 is fixed.

Adversarial probe, 8 constructs fed to all 11 checks. ALL 11 CHECKS EXIT 1 -- every
construct escapes. These are NEW, distinct from the gen0 set:

N1  if (driver.name === "LocalDriver")
    CHECK 8 covers only the switch form; CHECK 2 requires a lowercase quoted cloud/local.
N2  const { kind } = driver; if (kind === "local")
    destructuring removes the receiver CHECK 3a requires.
N3  if (driver?.kind === "local")
    optional chaining breaks CHECK 3a's word-boundary receiver-dot-kind pattern.
N4  if (driver["kind"] === "local")
    bracket access, no dot.
N5  if (Reflect.get(driver, "kind") === "local")
    no member expression at all.
N6  if (driver.isLocal)
    boolean capability flag, no discriminant comparison.
N7  if (driver.mode === "local")
    field name outside the enumerated set.
N8  const Comp = isLocalDriver ? LocalPanel : CloudPanel
    component-selection ternary; CHECK 9 only matches ternaries inside dynamic import.

N8 is the most serious. REQ-EX-01 s3 forbids exactly this -- no RENDERING or behavior
branches on which driver is active -- and swapping a component by ternary is the
idiomatic way a React/TSX codebase commits that violation. A procedure that cannot see
it does not operationalize the scenario it claims to ratify.

Consequence for the ratification claim, not merely for coverage: the ADR asserts at line
20 that the greps detect all known driver-conditional mechanisms, and binds a binary
verdict to them at lines 100-101 (PASS = zero hits across all 10; FAIL definitive = any
hit). Zero hits is sound only if the detector is sound. With 8 trivial escapes the PASS
side is unsound, so s3 is not yet falsifiable-via-this-procedure as claimed. Note the
closed-world section already concedes brittleness -- if ROOT.4.5 uses different strings
the pattern must be updated -- which is an admission that the grep set is an open-ended
denylist.

Evidence to satisfy: EITHER (a) extend the checks to cover N1 through N8, with the
negative control extended and re-run showing each caught; OR (b) downgrade the claim
honestly -- state that grep is a necessary-not-sufficient screen, that zero hits is NOT
by itself a PASS, and name the typed or human complement that closes the gap (e.g.
ROOT.4.5 typing the driver handle so no discriminant field is reachable, making the
class structurally unrepresentable rather than merely un-grepped). Either discharges.
What does not discharge is retaining "detect all known mechanisms" plus a definitive
binary verdict over a denylist proven porous in 8 places.

## Finding 3 -- FACTORY EXCEPTION: DISCHARGED

ADR line 92 now reads PARKED UNTIL ROOT.4.5, and: until then, NO EXCEPTIONS -- any hit in
any file is a FAIL. The gen0 self-declaring language (the or-equivalent factory path, and
the clause letting any file branch if its sole purpose is driver selection) is gone.
Lines 94-97 give an ADR-0028-style additive amendment procedure requiring a single named
file path plus exported symbol, a factory-pattern justification, and recording of the
amending item ID and date. Line 101 makes FAIL definitive until that amendment exists.
The residual illustrative path inside the PARKED block is an example, not a grant. No
residual self-declared exception language found.

## Finding 4 -- RE-RUN OWNER: DISCHARGED

Re-run binding section, lines 173-181, names both owners: ROOT.4.5 as acceptance-criterion
owner (MUST run all 10 checks and record results) and the ROOT.4.9 Phase 3 Gate as
gate-row owner. Line 175 states the vacuity honestly rather than hiding it. Line 181
routes mirroring into the ROOT.4.5 and ROOT.4.9 item files to the director, correctly
recognizing the implementer lacks write access there. Caveat, not a blocker: both
bindings inherit the 2a defect -- they re-run a script whose CHECK 8 under-detects.

## Acceptance criterion 2 -- no-edit ruling: STILL HOLDS

Shard untouched. The execution-layer shard mtime is 2026-07-25T08:23:21-04:00, predating
all ROOT.7.3.7 work (2026-07-27/28); the ADR mtime is 2026-07-27T23:01:20. A content
probe over the shard for ADR-0025, the item ID, and the word grep returns exit 1 -- no
ratification apparatus leaked into the spec. REQ-EX-01 s3 text at shard line 21 is
verbatim what the ADR quotes at line 167. Ruling correct: the scenario needs no edit;
the procedure belongs in the ADR. Per reviewer constraints I did not invoke git; mtime
plus content probe is the substitute evidence.

## Summary

finding 1 executable procedure ....... DISCHARGED
finding 2 pattern completeness ....... NOT DISCHARGED (2a divergence; 2b 8 new escapes)
finding 3 factory exception .......... DISCHARGED
finding 4 re-run owner ............... DISCHARGED
ac2 no-edit ruling ................... HOLDS

Three of four gen0 findings are genuinely fixed and the gen0 9-of-10 escape is closed.
Blocking on finding 2 only.
AUDITEOF
